central_unknown: Whether Mercedes' recent upgrade regression has been resolved for Austin, and whether Max Verstappen can reassert dominance at a circuit that historically favors Red Bull — ML projects him P1 finish from P3 quali, but the gap to Russell/Leclerc is tight.

budget_tiers.fills: Hadjar or Hulkenberg as budget driver

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 25.1 exp pts, 37.8 proj pts, ppm 1.81, MEDIUM risk. Predicted to qualify P3 and finish P1, giving position-gain upside. Historically dominant at COTA. Channels consistently rank him as the top captain option when he's expected to win on Sunday. Best ceiling on the grid with 90% CI up to 51.0 pts.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: ML projects 23.4 exp pts, 29.3 proj pts, ppm 0.68, MEDIUM risk. Predicted P4 quali → P2 finish. Channels note Russell has been inconsistent after Mercedes' upgrade regression in Malaysia, but ML still ranks him #2 on expected points. Lower ppm than Verstappen (0.68 vs 1.81) makes him a riskier captain. Worth considering if you already own him and want to avoid transfer penalties.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: ML projects 9.9 exp pts, ppm 1.21, solid value tier driver. Channels consistently flag him as a must-have budget builder — needs very few points for price rises. Predicted P8 quali → P8 finish with upside in chaotic races.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Channels highlight Lindblad as a no-brainer budget builder at the price floor. Has shown flashes of strong pace (SQ1 surprise in Singapore). Easy price-rise candidate needing minimal points.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: Channels flag Lawson as an underrated differential — under 5% ownership in top 500. Recent form: 12, 25, 16, 3, 17 pts across last 5 races. COTA could suit his aggressive style. Strong price-rise candidate.

consider.name: Nico Hulkenberg
consider.note: At price floor — cannot lose value. In ~96% of top 500 teams per channel data. Safe budget anchor. ML has Audi at 14.9 exp pts as constructor, so some baseline scoring expected.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: Channels note Alonso performs well at low-speed-corner tracks but explicitly flag COTA as 'probably not an ideal option' for Aston Martin. Sub-1% ownership makes him a pure differential punt. High risk.

consider.name: Sergio Perez
consider.note: Channels describe him as a 'transfer target/transfer trap' — ultra-cheap at 3M but DNF-prone. Could work in mega-team builds pairing with Verstappen + Red Bull constructor. Channels warn to have a plan to exit quickly.

avoid: Carlos Sainz — 13M price for predicted P18, terrible value per ML and channels
Valtteri Bottas — reliability concerns, DNF history, channels explicitly warn against despite price floor
Franco Colapinto — channels suggest replacing with Lawson or Hadjar if at awkward price point

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No channel explicitly recommends Wildcard for Austin. Non-sprint weekend limits chip value. Better saved for a triple-header or race with clearer scoring separation.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: Channels used 3x at Monza when Mercedes dominated — similar logic could apply if Mercedes/Verstappen look dominant after FP sessions. ML shows Verstappen at 37.8 proj pts and Antonelli at 23.5, so a 3x on Verstappen could yield ~75 pts. Wait for FP data before committing.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Channels note Limitless scored lower than 3x in recent simulations. Better saved for a sprint weekend or round with extreme budget constraints.

chips.name: 4A (Final Fix)
chips.reason: Channels recommend 4A when constructor scoring is tightly bunched. ML has Mercedes (60.8), Ferrari (51.9), Red Bull (46.5), McLaren (43.8) — all viable. Could final-fix a constructor after qualifying to optimize. Consider if you can run Mercedes + Ferrari base and final-fix to Red Bull if Verstappen qualifies strongly.

watch_items: Mercedes upgrade status — channels note regression after Malaysia upgrades; check if older Baku-spec aero or newer package is run at COTA
Verstappen qualifying position — ML predicts P3 quali but P1 finish; if he qualifies higher, captain value increases further
Antonelli FP pace — ML predicts P1 quali but only P4 finish (pred 21.6 exp pts); watch if Mercedes race pace confirms or if quali flattered
Weather at COTA — rain could shuffle the order significantly and boost safety-car-dependent drivers like Lindblad and Lawson
Hulkenberg reliability — gearbox issue flagged in Singapore sprint qualifying; monitor FP sessions for recurring mechanical problems
Red Bull constructor value — ML projects 46.5 exp pts at 32.7M vs Mercedes 60.8 at 34.0M; Red Bull cheaper but significantly lower floor
arc: Austin marks a critical inflection point in the season with only a handful of races remaining. Budget building enters its final phase — channels stress loading up on price-rise candidates like Hadjar, Lindblad, and Lawson now to maximize budget for the season-ending stretch through Mexico, Brazil, and Abu Dhabi. The Mercedes upgrade trajectory is the key storyline: if the older Baku aero specification proves competitive at COTA (as it did for Russell's Baku win), Mercedes remains the top constructor play through the Americas swing. If not, a pivot to Ferrari + Red Bull constructors may be needed for Mexico. Chip deployment becomes increasingly urgent — any unused 3x or Limitless chips should ideally be played within the next 2-3 races to avoid wasting them. Watch Verstappen's form closely; if he dominates Austin, he becomes the locked-in captain through the final rounds.
